1\. Role kits can rewrite the playbook by changing its case 🐞 Bug ⛨ Security 
Spool.stored_kit_playbooks (and kit._owner_warning) recognise only the exact names
PLAYBOOK.toml and meta/PLAYBOOK.toml, so an entry such as playbook.toml, Playbook.toml or
Meta/PLAYBOOK.toml passes _carries_no_playbook and the engine approves the apply. On a
case-insensitive filesystem the apply's unzip -o writes that entry over the real playbook, which
the apply then commits. The role can therefore raise its own max_architect_consults, drop a stop
rule or change the kickoff without the human seeing it, which is exactly what H-075 was meant to
stop.
Agent Prompt ``` ## Issue description The §43 hold detects a carried playbook by exact name, so a kit entry like `playbook.toml` or `Meta/PLAYBOOK.toml` is approved by the engine. On a case-folding filesystem it then overwrites the playbook in force. ## Fix Focus Areas - src/hands/spool.py[574-583] - src/hands/kit.py[873-900] ## Recommended Fix Compare each zip name with `name.casefold()` against `{p.casefold() for p in PLAYBOOK_PATHS}`, and return the entry name actually found. Apply the same case-folded match in `_owner_warning`. Add tests for `playbook.toml` and `Meta/PLAYBOOK.toml` being held. ``` ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools
